speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing. To help me understand your condition, have these episodes occurred while you are awake or when you are asleep?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient describes staring, facial grimacing, and post-ictal confusion, which is highly suggestive of a seizure; however, could you clarify if these episodes ever involve a loss of bladder control or turning blue? REQUEST TEST: EEG.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy

The EEG findings of interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the right temporal lobe, combined with your description of staring, facial grimacing, and post-ictal confusion, confirm a diagnosis of temporal lobe epilepsy. Multiple sclerosis does not fit this clinical picture.
